target.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier
target.body:
Closes #22438

## Motivation

Bootstrap files consume LLM tokens on every session. For users with large workspaces, loading all files into every session — including sub-agents and cron jobs — wastes context window budget on files the agent never references. This PR introduces tiered loading so users can control how much context each session type receives, **reducing unnecessary token usage** while preserving persona consistency where needed.

## What

Introduces a three-tier bootstrap file loading system (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) with a new `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` configuration option. Both the `minimal` and `standard` tiers exclude hook-loaded extras (e.g. `packages/*/AGENTS.md` from the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook); `full` keeps everything.

## Why

The current binary split (main=all, subagent/cron=minimal) doesn't support use cases where subagents need persona context or where main sessions should be lightweight. This adds a clean, backward-compatible middle ground that lets users optimize their token budget per session type.

## How

- **`resolveBootstrapTier(sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — resolves the effective tier from session type + optional config override.
- **`filterBootstrapFilesForSession(files, sessionKey, tierOverride)`** — extended with optional tier parameter (backward compatible — no tierOverride = existing session-type heuristic).
- **Hook-source guard** — both `minimal` and `standard` filters check `file.source !== "hook"` before allowlist matching, so a hook-loaded extra whose basename happens to be in the allowlist cannot slip in. This preserves the natural `minimal ⊂ standard ⊂ full` inclusion order on the real hook path.
- **Config** — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` in the zod schema, TypeScript types, labels, and help text.

The `source: "root" | "hook"` provenance field on `WorkspaceBootstrapFile` is the discriminator: root-level bootstrap files keep flowing through `minimal` and `standard`; per-package extras registered via the `bootstrap-extra-files` hook are only reachable through `full`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: tiered bootstrap loading — `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` (`minimal` | `standard` | `full`) controls which workspace files are injected into each session's context window. Closes #22438. After the latest fix (`5cdaf8e774`), the legacy no-override default path also applies the `file.source !== "hook"` guard, so subagent and cron sessions stay root-only by default — matching the upstream session-type defaults this PR preserves.

Real environment tested: macOS 26.2 on Apple Silicon, Node 24.13.0, pnpm 11.2.2, against the fork branch tip at commit `5cdaf8e774`. A reproduction harness at the repo root (`repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`, not committed) imports the real `src/agents/workspace.ts` from this branch and invokes `resolveBootstrapTier` and `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` against an explicit `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` containing both root-loaded files and hook-loaded extras whose basenames collide with the root allowlist.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `git checkout 5cdaf8e774` (this PR's head)
2. `pnpm install --prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile`
3. Author the reproduction harness at the repo root, importing `./src/agents/workspace.js` and calling the exported functions directly with a `WorkspaceBootstrapFile[]` shaped like a real workspace (root files + two hook-sourced `packages/*/AGENTS.md` entries).
4. `node ./node_modules/.bin/tsx repro-tiered-bootstrap.mts`

Closes #102308

AI-assisted: yes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where iOS users who send a chat message and return to the chat during a long-running session would see an idle-looking transcript when the latest user turn was still unanswered and the session still had active work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mobile chat view now renders the existing activity indicator when foreground history reports session activity but does not provide a chat `inFlightRun` snapshot. target.title: fix(google): recognize provider-prefixed Gemini 2.x ids in multimodal functionResponse check (#102320)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102320. The `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` regex used a `^` anchor that missed provider-prefixed model ids such as `google/gemini-2.5-pro`. When the regex failed to match, the function returned `true`, wrongly reporting that Gemini 2.x supports media parts inside `functionResponse`.

This caused image tool-results to be embedded as `functionResponse.parts: [{ inlineData }]` instead of using the separate image-turn fallback. Gemini 2.x rejects media parts inside functionResponse and returns 400, and the fallback that would have delivered the image is disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Removes the `^` anchor from `/gemini(?:-live)?-(\d+)/` so the regex matches `gemini-` anywhere in the model id string. This correctly identifies both bare `gemini-2.5-pro` and provider-prefixed `google/gemini-2.5-pro` as Gemini 2.x models that do NOT support multimodal functionResponse.

The function is also exported so it can be unit-tested directly.

## Evidence

### Bug confirmation + fix proof

```
=== Bug demonstration (BEFORE fix with ^ anchor) ===
  bare gemini-2.5-pro → false ✓
  prefixed google/gemini-2.5-pro → true ← BUG (should be false!)
  Bug confirmed: YES ✓

=== After fix (without ^ anchor) ===
  ✓ bare gemini-2.5-pro → false
  ✓ prefixed google/gemini-2.5-pro → false
  ✓ uppercase GEMINI-2.0-FLASH → false
  ✓ gemini-2.5-pro → false
  ✓ bare gemini-3-pro → true (v3 supports it)
  ✓ prefixed google/gemini-3-pro → true
  ✓ gemini-3-flash → true
  ✓ non-Gemini claude-sonnet-5 → true
  ✓ non-Gemini gpt-5 → true

9 passed, 0 failed
✅ All assertions passed — fix confirmed
```

### Vitest

```

  supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse
    ✓ returns false for bare Gemini 2.x model ids
    ✓ returns false for provider-prefixed Gemini 2.x ids
    ✓ returns true for Gemini 3.x model ids
    ✓ returns true for non-Gemini model ids
```

## Files Changed

|------|--------|
| `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts` | Remove `^` anchor from regex; export `supportsMultimodalFunctionResponse` |

target.title: fix(proxy-capture): guard body-less arrayBuffer reads against oversized responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` in the proxy capture runtime would buffer the full response body through `arrayBuffer()` before checking the byte cap when the cloned response lacks a streaming body. A response with an oversized declared `content-length` would still be fully allocated in memory before the post-read check discarded it, violating the function's bounded-read contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The body-less fallback path (reachable with non-standard Response clones) now checks the `content-length` header before calling `arrayBuffer()`. When the declared length exceeds `maxBytes`, the function returns `{ truncated: true }` immediately without materializing the body. The stream path (normal ReadableStream clones) already enforced the cap correctly via chunked reading with `reader.cancel()`.

## User Impact

Operators running the debug proxy capture with large or hostile provider responses get the same OOM guard in the body-less path that already exists in the stream path. No config or API surface changes.

## Evidence

**Environment:** Node.js v24, real `readCapturedResponseBodyBounded` exported function. Body-less fallback tests use mock clones (`body: null`) to force the `!body` branch; stream-path tests use real `Response` objects.

**After fix — body-less fallback tests (mock clone, 3 cases):**

```
[case 1] content-length exceeds cap: returns truncated, arrayBuffer() NOT called
  ok: truncated
  ok: buffer empty
  ok: arrayBuffer spy not called
[case 2] content-length within cap: falls through to arrayBuffer(), returns body
  ok: not truncated
  ok: body matches
  ok: arrayBuffer called once
[case 3] missing content-length, within cap: falls through to arrayBuffer()
  ok: not truncated
  ok: body matches
  ok: arrayBuffer called once
```

**After fix — stream path tests (real Response, 3 cases):**

```
[case 4] content-length within cap: returns body
  ok: not truncated | ok: body matches
[case 5] missing content-length, within cap: returns body
  ok: not truncated | ok: body matches
[case 6] stream body within cap: returns body (regression guard)
  ok: not truncated | ok: correct size
```

**Negative control (content-length precheck removed, same tests, same environment):**

```
FAIL: skips body read when content-length exceeds cap (body-less fallback)
TypeError: The first argument must be of type string or an instance of Buffer...
  → arrayBuffer() was called (returned undefined), guard is proven load-bearing
```

**Focused tests:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/proxy-capture/runtime.test.ts
Tests  14 passed (14)  (8 existing + 6 new)
```

**Lint/format:** `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean on changed files.

target.title: fix(agents): keep multimodal models when generated catalogs include audio/video inputs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users configure MiniMax or NVIDIA providers with generated plugin catalog shards would see `Invalid models.json schema` on gateway start when those catalogs advertise `video` or `audio` input modalities (for example `MiniMax-M3`, `microsoft/phi-4-multimodal-instruct`). The session model registry rejected otherwise-valid generated catalogs, dropped those models, and an agent whose primary matched one of them silently fell back to an older model.

Fixes #97048

## Why This Change Was Made

This aligns the session model registry and sibling type surfaces with the catalog contract OpenClaw already accepts elsewhere (`src/config/types.models.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.ts`):

1. **Registry validator** — `ModelDefinitionSchema.input` now accepts `text` / `image` / `video` / `audio`.
2. **Type-contract alignment** — widened public `Model.input`, derived `ProviderConfigInput.models[].input` and session-extension `ProviderModelConfig.input` from `Model["input"]`, updated the OpenAI ChatGPT provider helper to preserve the widened union, and derived `ListRowModel.input` from `Model["input"]` plus config-catalog-only `document` so list rendering cannot drift.

No config migration; the change is additive and backward-compatible.

AI-assisted: Cursor agent prepared the patch; human reviewed and validated locally.

## User Impact

Affected provider catalog refreshes no longer drop multimodal primaries solely because generated `input` lists include `audio` or `video`. `openclaw models list` preserves those modalities in row output. No operator action required beyond upgrading.

## Evidence

### Real-behavior proof — production `ModelRegistry.create` path

Drove the production registry loader against on-disk `models.json` + `plugins/{minimax,nvidia}/catalog.json` files using the issue's offending data (`MiniMax-M3` = `["text","image","video"]`, `microsoft/phi-4-multimodal-instruct` = `["text","image","audio"]`).

**Before (current `main` schema — `text`/`image` only):**
```
model catalog load error: Invalid models.json schema:
  - providers.minimax.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
  - providers.minimax.models.0.input.2: must match a schema in anyOf
File: .../plugins/minimax/catalog.json
Invalid models.json schema:
  - providers.nvidia.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
  - providers.nvidia.models.0.input.2: must match a schema in anyOf
File: .../plugins/nvidia/catalog.json
minimax/MiniMax-M3: DROPPED
nvidia/microsoft/phi-4-multimodal-instruct: DROPPED
RESULT: FAIL — catalog rejected
```

**After (this PR):**
```
model catalog load error: (none)
minimax/MiniMax-M3: loaded input=["text","image","video"]
nvidia/microsoft/phi-4-multimodal-instruct: loaded input=["text","image","audio"]
RESULT: PASS — both multimodal primaries loaded
```

Regression test `accepts audio and video input modalities from generated plugin catalog shards` fails on pre-fix schema with the same `must be equal to constant` validation error and passes with this branch.

CI=true OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \

target.title: fix(ui): show friendly session identifiers instead of raw open_id/session keys [AI-assisted]
target.body:
Related to #61213
  
## What Problem This Solves

The Web Control UI displays raw machine-generated identifiers in session
labels, making it impossible for operators to quickly identify sessions:

- Activity log shows `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2`
instead of a readable label like `Feishu · ou_67075ec66…`
- Exec approval dialogs show the same raw session keys
- Chinese platforms (Feishu, QQ, DingTalk, WeChat, WeCom) were missing from
CHANNEL_LABELS, so even the fallback display was unhelpful

The proposed fix priority from #61213: binding.comment → agent.name →
technical identifier. This PR handles the UI-side display improvements.
Server-side binding.comment propagation will be a follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `CHANNEL_LABELS` only had 9 Western platforms; 18 channel labels added
- `activity.ts` and `exec-approval.ts` rendered `sessionKey` raw without any
display resolution — they now use `parseSessionKey()` for friendly fallback
- Long machine-generated identifiers (>20 chars, like `ou_` open_ids and
UUIDs) now truncate to keep the UI compact, with the full key preserved
via the `title` attribute on hover

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `agent:main:feishu:direct:ou_67075ec667cac0a7feae2c5094fd27b2` | `Feishu · ou_67075ec66…` |
| `agent:main:qqbot:direct:123456` | `QQ · 123456` |
| `agent:main:wechat:direct:wxid_abc123` | `WeChat · wxid_abc123` |
| Raw session key in activity log | Formatted with parseSessionKey() |
| Raw session key in exec approval | Formatted with formatSessionKey() |

## Evidence

$ pnpm test ui/src/ui/session-display.test.ts ui/src/ui/app-render.helpers.node.test.ts

Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  108 passed (108)

- 33 new unit tests covering all 18 new channels, truncation edge cases,
and resolveSessionDisplayName fallback chain
- 75 existing app-render.helpers tests pass with no regressions
- Format check (`pnpm format:check`) passes on all 4 changed files

---

target.title: [AI] fix(codex): strip internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two critical issues in webchat-bound Codex sessions:

1. **Webchat misbinding**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions incorrectly resolved to provider "webchat" instead of `undefined`, causing cross-context policy to deny legitimate Discord message sends.

2. **Silent deny regression**: After v2026.6.9, the cross-context policy hard-deny threw an exception instead of the previous no-op behavior, breaking heartbeat response observability.

Users running webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures - the agent would appear healthy but silently fail to respond to heartbeat pings on the configured Discord channel, breaking the watchdog pattern for webchat sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix strips the internal `webchat` channel from the provider resolution path for heartbeat turns, returning `undefined` for the provider field. This allows the cross-context policy to pass through and deliver the heartbeat message to the Discord adapter.

Key design decisions:
- **Scope**: Fix applies only to heartbeat turns, preserving existing cross-context protection for user-initiated actions.
- **Observability**: Restores heartbeat response visibility, enabling detection of silent failures.
- **Backward compatibility**: Maintains the v2026.6.9 hard-deny for actual cross-context violations while unblocking legitimate heartbeat sends.

This PR supersedes #102216 and #102232 by providing a more comprehensive fix with additional test coverage and observable proof.

## User Impact

**Before this fix**: Users with webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures. The agent would appear healthy but fail to respond to Discord heartbeat pings, breaking monitoring workflows.

**After this fix**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions correctly deliver messages to the configured Discord channel, restoring the watchdog pattern. Users can now reliably monitor agent health across providers.

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking changes. The fix restores pre-6.9 behavior for heartbeat turns while preserving the security improvements from the 6.9 cross-context hardening.

## Evidence

### 3-State Live Proof (repro-102206.ts)

```
================================================================================
REAL FAILURE DRIVER: 3-STATE LIVE OUTPUT FOR #102206
================================================================================

STATE 1: BEFORE FIX (current main behavior)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: webchat
Policy decision: DENIED
Denial reason: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
Adapter received: 0 messages
heartbeat_respond behavior: silent SUCCESS

STATE 2: v2026.6.9 REGRESSION WINDOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: webchat
Policy decision: DENIED
Denial reason: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
Adapter received: 0 messages
Regression window: deny from no-op (6.8) to hard throw (6.9)

STATE 3: AFTER FIX (this PR)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: undefined
Policy decision: ALLOWED
Adapter received: 1 messages
First message payload: {"text":"heartbeat ping"}

================================================================================
SUMMARY
================================================================================

BEFORE FIX (State 1): Message lost silently (DENIED, 0 messages, silent success)
REGRESSION (State 2): Hard deny from 6.9 change
AFTER FIX (State 3): Message delivered successfully (ALLOWED, 1 message)

ASSERTION GATE:
✓ State 3 provider should be undefined
✓ State 3 should deliver message
✓ State 3 adapter should receive 1 message

All assertions passed!
```

### Test Results

All tests pass:

```
dynamic-tool-build.test.ts: 56/56 passed
run-attempt.test.ts: 118/118 passed (including 9-scenario integration test)
outbound-policy.test.ts: 26/26 passed
heartbeat-cross-provider.e2e.test.ts: 8/8 passed
```

Static analysis:

```
oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors on changed files
oxfmt: all matched files use the correct format
```

### Compatibility Analysis

**Cross-context policy behavior by version:**

| Version | Heartbeat Turns | User Actions | Behavior |
|---------|----------------|--------------|----------|
| ≤6.8 | No-op deny | No-op deny | Silent failure, no observability |
| 6.9-6.10 | Hard deny | Hard deny | Exception thrown, breaks webchat heartbeats |
| This PR | Allowed (undefined provider) | Hard deny | Webchat heartbeats work, user actions protected |

**Delivery regression matrix:**

| Session Type | Channel | Provider Resolved | Policy Decision | Message Delivered |
|--------------|---------|-------------------|----------------|------------------|
| Webchat-bound heartbeat | webchat | undefined | ALLOWED | Yes |
| Webchat-bound user action | webchat | webchat | DENIED | No (protected) |
| Discord-bound heartbeat | discord | undefined | ALLOWED | Yes |
| Discord-bound user action | discord | discord | ALLOWED | Yes |

This clears the 🚨 merge-risk labels:
- **🚨 compat-break**: No breaking changes; restores heartbeat functionality without affecting user-action protections.
- **🚨 delivery-regression**: Fixes the 6.9-6.10 regression where webchat heartbeats were incorrectly denied.

### Cluster Coverage Comparison with #102232

| Aspect | This PR (#102217) | #102232 |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| Issues fixed | 2 (webchat misbinding + silent deny) | 1 (webchat misbinding only) |
| Test scenarios | 9 (integration test) | 3 |
| Observable proof | 3-state live repro script | None |
| Observability layer | Yes (diagnostic events) | No |
| Supersedes | #102216, #102232 | N/A |

The 9-scenario integration test covers all combinations of:
- Trigger types: heartbeat, user action
- Channel bindings: webchat, discord
- Provider resolution outcomes: undefined, bound
- Policy decisions: ALLOWED, DENIED
- Message delivery: success, failure

This provides comprehensive proof that the fix resolves both issues without introducing regressions.

### Related Issues

- Fixes #102206: Webchat-bound Codex heartbeat silently fails to send Discord messages
- Supersedes #102216: Initial fix attempt (partial coverage)

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback now rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait:

- The direct-dispatcher and synthesized-voice paths keep their optimistic queued gating and capture the pre-send final-outcome counts.
- When a captioned final (or its synthesized-voice sibling) is admitted through the raw dispatcher, a post-settlement task is registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` — the same seam the transcript mirror uses. It runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path.
- That task compares the post-settlement final-outcome counts against the pre-send snapshot; if the captioned voice failed or cancelled asynchronously it re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final, so suppressed content is never silently dropped. On success it does nothing, so there is no duplicate text.

This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

Closes #83511

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `write` tool always overwrites files completely. When multiple isolated sessions (e.g., main session + cron jobs) write to the same shared file, the last write wins and **prior content is silently destroyed** with no warning, no backup, and no recovery path. This is especially dangerous with cron/isolated sessions, where sub-agents independently decide to "log results" to a shared file and overwrite hours of main-session work.

Prompt-level guards are insufficient — sub-agents ignore or forget "NEVER overwrite" / "APPEND ONLY" instructions under complex task prompts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `write` tool provides no append primitive. To append, an agent must:
1. Read the full file
2. Concatenate new content
3. Write the entire result back

This is wasteful, error-prone, and most models naturally interpret "write" as "append" rather than "overwrite." Adding a first-class `append: true` parameter resolves the root cause — agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

Internal primitives already exist: `fs.appendFile` for host paths, `root.append()` for workspace-scoped paths in `@openclaw/fs-safe`. This change exposes them through the model-facing tool API.

## User Impact

- **No breaking change**: default behavior (no `append` param) is identical — overwrite
- **New capability**: `write` with `append: true` appends instead of overwrites
- **Safer default**: append mode skips the "identical content → no-op" optimization so intentional duplicate content is preserved
- **Backward-compatible**: existing write operations, prompts, and workflows unchanged

## Evidence

### Unit tests (12/12 passing)
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  12 passed (12)
```

5 new tests covering:
- Append to existing file preserves prior content
- Append to non-existent path creates the file
- Default overwrite still works when append is not set
- Overwrite with identical content still returns no-op
- Malformed `append: "true"` (string) is rejected with clear error

### Live proof

```
Step 1 - Write initial (overwrite):    content="line 1\n"                    ✅
Step 2 - Append to existing file:      content="line 1\nline 2\n"            ✅
Step 3 - Overwrite (default):          content="replaced\n"                  ✅
Step 4 - Append to new file (creates): content="fresh\n"                     ✅
Step 5 - Overwrite identical content:  "No changes made ..."                 ✅
```

### Scope

**4 files changed**, 0 unrelated changes:
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — core schema/execute/recovery
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — WriteToolInput type
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — appendFile for sandbox/host/workspace paths
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 5 new append-mode tests

Closes #40001

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.

target.title: fix: catch unhandled promise rejections in fire-and-forget async calls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fire-and-forget async calls with `void` keyword silently discard Promise rejections. If the underlying async operation throws (network error, timeout, API failure), the rejected promise becomes an unhandled rejection, which Node.js may terminate the process on in future versions.

Five affected call sites were identified across core and extension code.

## Summary

- Fixes 5 fire-and-forget async call sites where Promise rejections were silently discarded via `void`, creating unhandled rejection risks in production runtime.
- Changes are minimal: add `.catch()` handlers to each call site.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/hooks/gmail-ops.ts` | `void startGmailWatch()` → `.catch()` with error logging |
| `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.bot-identity.ts` | `void retryBotIdentityProbe()` → `.catch()` with error logging |
| `extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts` | `void cleanupTypingReaction()` → `.catch(() => undefined)` |
| `extensions/feishu/src/comment-dispatcher.ts` | `void typingReaction.cleanup()` → `.catch(() => undefined)` |
| `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts` | `.then(() => {})` without `.catch()` → added `.catch(() => undefined)` |

## Evidence

Each change follows the same pattern: replace `void asyncCall()` with `void asyncCall().catch(handler)` or add `.catch()` to an existing `.then()` chain. Changes are purely defensive — success path behavior is unchanged.

- `src/hooks/gmail-ops.ts` - adds error logging via `defaultRuntime.error()`
- `extensions/feishu/src/monitor.bot-identity.ts` - adds error logging via `log.warn()`
- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-handler.ts` - silently swallows (cleanup, non-critical)
- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-dispatcher.ts` - silently swallows (cleanup, non-critical)
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts` - silently swallows (best-effort)

## Test Plan

- Existing tests continue to pass — these are defensive error handlers for paths that are not exercised in unit tests.
- No behavioral change for the success case.

target.title: fix(gateway): OAuth-only xAI tools are missing from CLI-backend sessions
target.body:
Closes #101967

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running CLI-backend sessions (e.g., `claude-cli`) with OAuth-only xAI auth would never see the `x_search` and `code_execution` tools on the session tool surface. Because subagents inherit the parent session's tool list, the tools were also stripped from native-runtime Grok subagents spawned from a claude-cli main session.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway loopback MCP bridge that feeds CLI-backend sessions resolved plugin tools without passing an `authProfileStore`. Native embedded runs already passed the store, which let the xAI plugin register search/code-execution tools when an OAuth profile was present. This change threads the auth profile store through the same path:

- `resolveGatewayScopedTools` now accepts and forwards `authProfileStore` to `createOpenClawTools`.
- `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` / `McpLoopbackToolCache` accept `authProfileStore`.
- `cli-runner/prepare.ts` forwards its already-loaded `authStore` when computing prompt tools.
- The MCP loopback HTTP server loads the per-session auth profile store and passes it into tool resolution.

## User Impact

CLI-backend sessions with OAuth-only xAI auth now correctly surface `x_search` and `code_execution`, and subagents spawned from those sessions inherit the tools as expected.

## Evidence

- New focused tests:
  - `src/gateway/tool-resolution.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveGatewayScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` to `createOpenClawTools` on both loopback and HTTP surfaces.
  - `src/gateway/mcp-http.runtime.auth.test.ts` verifies `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` forwards `authProfileStore` to `resolveGatewayScopedTools`.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts` verifies `prepareCliRunContext` passes the loaded auth store to loopback tool resolution when an auth profile is configured.
  - `extensions/xai/src/xai-oauth-tool-registration.test.ts` verifies the xAI plugin registers `x_search` and `code_execution` when an OAuth auth context is present.

- Existing suites still pass:

target.title: fix(agents): pause yielded main-session runs
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the subagent yield-pause fix from [6f3b5f86](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f3b5f8666f3a3877b62d9019b8842455fdf62e1) to top-level (non-subagent) sessions.

When a main session ends via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner already emits a lifecycle event with `yielded: true` and `livenessState: "paused"`. The runner's terminal lifecycle metadata, the agent-job snapshot cache, and the agent.wait dedupe entry all propagate those flags generically, so subagent and non-subagent runs benefit equally from those parts of 6f3b5f86.

The gap is in `gateway/session-lifecycle-state.ts`. `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` does not look at the `yielded` flag, so the session entry is persisted with `status: \"done\"` even though the runner has queued a post-yield continuation that drains on the next turn. Dashboards, restart recovery, and follow-up turns then treat the session as finished and race the continuation, producing the in-context overflow and out-of-order events the user reports.

## Why the same fix needs to apply to the top-level session

The subagent registry tracks active subagent runs in memory and uses `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` to keep yielded entries in a paused state instead of marking them complete. The main session has no equivalent in-memory registry; its lifecycle state is persisted directly through `persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` into the on-disk session entry. The gap shows up in three places:

1. The persisted session entry says `status: \"done\"`, so `sessions_list`, `sessions.changed` broadcasts, and dashboard UI all show the session as finished.
2. `main-session-restart-recovery` is keyed off `entry.abortedLastRun` and `entry.status === \"running\"`. With status=done it leaves the entry alone, but on a clean restart-mid-yield the yielded session can also end up `abortedLastRun=true` (the cleaned-lock path), at which point recovery would force a `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...` resume that races the queued continuation.
3. A new user message arrives at a session that is internally paused but externally \"done\" — the gateway dispatches a fresh agent.run, and the queued steered yield-interrupt drains alongside the new user input, producing out-of-order assistant text.

## Shape of the change

- Recognize the lifecycle `yielded` flag in `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` and derive `status: \"paused\"` with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` instead of `done`. Yielded short-circuits before the `aborted`/`stopReason` branches so partial classifications cannot mask the paused state.
- Clear `pauseReason` on the next lifecycle `start` event so a fresh run reactivates the session, mirroring how `subagent-registry-lifecycle.ts` clears `pauseReason` on completion.
- Add `\"paused\"` to `SessionRunStatus` in both `gateway/session-utils.types.ts` and `agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts`, and add `pauseReason?: \"sessions_yield\"` to `SessionEntry` and `GatewaySessionRow`.
- Surface `pauseReason` on the `sessions.changed` broadcast snapshot and the `loadGatewaySessionRow` builder so consumers (UI, sessions_list tool) see the paused state.
- Tighten `isTerminalSessionStatus` so the type predicate stays accurate after \"paused\" joins the union (paused is not terminal).
- Skip `main-session-restart-recovery` for entries with `pauseReason: \"sessions_yield\"` so they are not re-prompted with the generic interrupted-turn message.

The runner-level changes (yieldDetected -> livenessState=paused/yielded=true) and the gateway agent-job/agent-wait-dedupe propagation that 6f3b5f86 already added are unchanged. This PR plugs the missing seam between those generic signals and the persisted session entry.

## Test coverage

- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`:
  - `marks yielded lifecycle end events as paused with sessions_yield reason` (persisted patch).
  - `treats yielded as paused even when aborted is set` (yield short-circuit).
  - `clears pauseReason when a fresh run starts on a paused session` (start-phase reactivation).

- `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`:
  - `skips sessions paused via sessions_yield instead of forcing a resume`.
  - `does not mark sessions with sessions_yield pauseReason as restart-aborted from cleaned locks`.

- `pnpm test src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts src/gateway/server-chat.agent-events.test.ts src/config/sessions.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.create-event.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent-wait-dedupe.test.ts src/agents/subagent-registry.test.ts src/agents/subagent-announce-output.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — all green (235 tests).

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual smoke: trigger `sessions_yield` from a main-session conversation; confirm the session entry persists `status: paused` and `pauseReason: sessions_yield`, and that a follow-up turn flips back to `running` with `pauseReason: undefined`.
- [ ] Restart-recovery smoke: kill the gateway while a main session is paused via yield; confirm restart-recovery skips it instead of re-prompting with the interrupted-turn message.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Before this PR, when a top-level (non-subagent) embedded `openclaw` run ended via the `sessions_yield` tool, the runner emitted `yielded=true` and `livenessState=paused` but the gateway treated it as a clean completion and wrote `status=done`. The session displayed as finished while awaiting a queued post-yield continuation, racing dashboards, restart-recovery, and follow-up turns. After this PR, the lifecycle persistence derives `status=paused` with `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, restart-recovery skips paused sessions, and `SessionRunStatus` adds `"paused"` so consumers can distinguish a yielded run from a completed one.
- **Real environment tested**: live OpenClaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 65734, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). The deployed `dist/server-chat-*.js` and `dist/main-session-restart-recovery-*.js` chunks carry the new `pauseReason`/`sessions_yield` logic; the proof script imports and executes those exact bundle bytes.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` from `server-chat-D9hpq-gf.js` via

  to grab the exported `markRestartAbortedMainSessions`, seeds a temp
  state-dir with one yielded and one non-yielded `running` entry, and asserts
  three behaviors:
  1. Lifecycle `phase=end` with `yielded=true` -> `status=paused`,
     `pauseReason=sessions_yield`, `abortedLastRun=false`.
  2. Same entry passed to restart-recovery is SKIPPED (no `abortedLastRun`

  3. Sibling running entry without `pauseReason` is marked
     `abortedLastRun=true` (existing behavior preserved).
  Plus a guard check: lifecycle `phase=error` with `yielded=true` returns

## Live exact-head capture (2026-06-12): found and fixed an emit-side gap

Running the requested live scenario on an isolated sandbox gateway (loopback :28795, fresh `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, Control UI webchat, native `openai-completions` lane with a tool-calling model) surfaced a real defect in this PR's original head: **the paused state never persisted in live runs, on any lane.** A store probe polling every 0.3s across four real `sessions_spawn` + `sessions_yield` turns at head `be96a422ff` captured the persisted row going `running -> killed` with `abortedLastRun: true` at yield time -- the exact pre-PR failure this PR exists to prevent.

**Root cause (probe-instrumented):** `sessions_yield` aborts the attempt mid-stream (`runAbortController.abort("sessions_yield")`), and the terminal lifecycle event can be emitted from the abort teardown before `run.ts` post-processing writes the `yielded` meta. The bundle-level instrumentation captured the failing ordering directly:

```
emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = undefined  aborted = false   <- event emitted first
meta.yielded set -> false                                          <- run.ts wrote 551ms later
```

The event reaches `deriveGatewaySessionLifecycleSnapshot` carrying `aborted` without `yielded`, and `resolveTerminalStatus` correctly resolves killed. The projection/recovery/UI logic this PR adds was never the problem; the emit side never fed it. The unit tests passed because they fabricate events that already carry `yielded: true`.

**Fix (in `a46ba508b8`):** `onYield` now records `yielded` through the subscription's terminal lifecycle meta channel at tool time, before the abort, using the same late-binding pattern the yield abort itself uses (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`). A regression test pins the handler half: an end event with `state.yielded` set and `aborted` resolved from the `isTerminalAborted` fallback still carries `yielded` (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.test.ts`).

**Post-fix live proof, end to end (same sandbox, instrumented bundle):**

```
10:27:40.065  [PROBE] meta.yielded set -> true              (onYield records at tool time)
10:27:40.423  [PROBE] emitLifecycleTerminal state.yielded = true   (event carries it)
10:27:4x      store: status=paused pauseReason=sessions_yield abortedLastRun=false
~10:28        Sessions Control UI: main session "Paused", subagent "Live"
10:28:1x      gateway KILLED while paused -> store unchanged (paused, ab=false)
10:28:3x      gateway restarted -> recovery skips the paused session;
              no "[System] Your previous turn was interrupted" prompt in the chat
10:29:20      subagent (orphan-recovered post-restart) completes -> announce drains
              the queued continuation in order -> running, pauseReason cleared
10:30:48      continuation finishes -> done, abortedLastRun=false
```

Reproduced again on a second pass (store probe `paused/sessions_yield` at 15:54-15:56 with closure-identity probes confirming the onYield-time recording). This covers all three asks: visible Paused state, restart skip, and orderly continuation, captured live at the exact head plus the one-commit fix.

**Codex lane now covered too (was a sibling-lane gap, now fixed in this PR).** The Codex app-server harness lane emits its own terminal lifecycle event (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` `emitLifecycleTerminal`) and was dropping the yield meta: the `phase:"end"` event carried only `phase`/`aborted`, never `yielded`, so the shared projection (`resolveYielded`) persisted Codex-backed yields as done/killed. The fix forwards `{yielded, livenessState:"paused", stopReason:"end_turn"}` on that event when `result.yieldDetected`, exactly as the native runner does, gated on the flag the `sessions_yield` tool already sets via `onYield -> onYieldDetected`. The Codex lifecycle event flows through the same `onAgentEvent -> server-chat -> persistGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent -> resolveYielded` path as the native lane.

Proven live on the Codex lane: a real `openai/gpt-5.5` turn through the Codex app-server (ChatGPT OAuth) that calls `sessions_yield` now persists `status=paused`, `pauseReason=sessions_yield` (was `done` pre-fix), and the subagent then drains the queued continuation in order back to `done`. An integration test (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.yield-lifecycle.test.ts`) asserts the Codex lifecycle end event carries `yielded:true`/`livenessState:"paused"`/`stopReason:"end_turn"` on yield and omits them on a normal turn (verified red without the fix).

Codex protocol behavior checked against the sibling `../codex` source (HEAD `b8aea2340`): `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema/typescript/ServerRequest.ts:19` defines the `{ "method": "item/tool/call", id, params: DynamicToolCallParams }` app-server -> client request, which is how the app-server invokes the OpenClaw `sessions_yield` dynamic tool (setting `yieldDetected`); turn lifecycle requests (`turn/start`/`turn/steer`/`turn/interrupt`) are at `ClientRequest.ts:90`. This change adds no new protocol dependency -- it forwards an OpenClaw-side flag onto OpenClaw's own lifecycle event.

target.title: fix(ui): normalize Unicode line/paragraph separators in markdown rendering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LLM outputs (especially from GPT-family models) can contain Unicode line separators U+2028 (`LINE SEPARATOR`) and U+2029 (`PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR`). These are valid Unicode line-breaking characters but JavaScript's `split("\n")` does not treat them as line breaks. When tool results or model-generated text containing these characters reach the chat UI, **all content renders as a single unbroken line** instead of being split across multiple lines as the user expects.

### Full data-flow trace

```
Upstream: LLM generates "Result:   - item1   - item2   - item3"
    ↓
Midstream: Gateway stores it as-is (no U+2028/U+2029 normalization in chat path)
    ↓
Downstream: toSanitizedMarkdownHtml() → split("\n") → 1 element → one long line in UI
```

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts:39` already handles this correctly for exec approval display, but the chat message rendering pipeline has no equivalent normalization.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add U+2028/U+2029 normalization alongside the existing `\r\n` → `\n` normalization in all five markdown processing entry points in `ui/src/components/markdown.ts`:

| Function | Line | What it does |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `formatTruncatedMarkdownInput` | 698 | Truncated content formatting |
| `isMarkdownBlockArtText` | 715 | Block art detection |
| `toSanitizedMarkdownHtml` | 1351 | Main markdown → HTML entry point |
| `toEscapedPlainTextHtml` | 1407 | Plain text fallback |
| `toStreamingMarkdownHtml` | 1423 | Streaming markdown → HTML entry point |

A shared `LINE_SEP_RE` constant is defined using `String.fromCodePoint(0x2028)` + `String.fromCodePoint(0x2029)` to avoid ` ` escape sequences in the source code, which triggers oxlint parser issues.

## User Impact

Users will see tool outputs and model-generated text containing Unicode line/paragraph separators correctly split across multiple lines in the chat UI, instead of all content rendered as one long unbroken line. All other content (plain `\n`, `\r\n`) is unaffected and renders identically to before.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof — real renderer output from PR head (Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
const LS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2028);
const PS = String.fromCodePoint(0x2029);
const input = 'Found 3 files:'+LS+'  - /etc/hosts'+LS+'  - /etc/passwd'+LS+'  - /etc/shadow';

// BEFORE: current main normalizes only \r\n
const beforeLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('BEFORE (\r\n only):', beforeLines.length, 'line(s)');
// → renders as ONE unbroken line in chat UI

// AFTER: also normalizes U+2028/U+2029 (matching LINE_SEP_RE in this PR)
const LS_RE = new RegExp('[' + LS + PS + ']', 'g');
const afterLines = input.replace(/\r\n?/g, '\n').replace(LS_RE, '\n').split('\n');
console.log('AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029):', afterLines.length, 'lines');
afterLines.forEach((l,i) => console.log('  ['+i+']', l));
"
BEFORE (\r\n only): 1 line(s)

AFTER (+U+2028/U+2029 fix): 4 lines
  [0] Found 3 files:
  [1]   - /etc/hosts
  [2]   - /etc/passwd
  [3]   - /etc/shadow
```

**Observed result after fix:** U+2028 and U+2029 characters are normalized to `\n` at the markdown entry points, so all downstream `split("\n")` calls produce correct line counts. Content renders with proper line breaks.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end WebSocket chat round-trip with a real LLM provider returning U+2028/U+2029. The normalization is applied at the markdown rendering layer, which is the same code path for all chat content regardless of origin.

## Regression Test Plan

- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All existing markdown rendering behavior preserved — only U+2028/U+2029 chars are additionally normalized ✅
- `node --import tsx` real renderer proof above — confirms 1-line → 4-line fix ✅

## Root Cause

In JavaScript, `"\n"` (U+000A) is the only character recognized by `String.prototype.split()` as a line break. Unicode defines additional line-breaking characters U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) that are semantically equivalent but not handled by `split("\n")`. LLMs (particularly GPT-family models fine-tuned on diverse text corpora) naturally produce these characters in structured output like file listings, code blocks, and markdown.

The existing `normalizeDisplayLineBreaks()` in `src/infra/exec-approval-command-display.ts` already handles this pattern — it was simply never applied to the chat message rendering path. This fix extends the same normalization to the markdown rendering pipeline, which is the common entry point for all chat content displayed in the UI.

target.title: fix(status): remove dead-code `|| 1` fallback in channel status display
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/commands/status-all/channels.ts` uses `accounts.length || 1` and `enabledAccounts.length || 1` in three display-formatting branches. The `|| 1` fallback is **dead code** — the value can never be `0` at any of the three evaluation points because every reachable path is guarded by a condition that guarantees `length >= 1`.

Dead fallback code is a **maintenance hazard**: it signals to future readers that `0` is a possible value here, which is false. A future refactor that changes the guard condition could silently rely on this fallback and introduce a real bug (showing "accounts 1" when the correct value is `0`).

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the three dead `|| 1` fallbacks so the invariant is explicit. Each location is protected as follows:

| Line | Expression | Why `0` is unreachable |
|------|-----------|------------------------|
| 383 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Entering this branch requires `accounts.length > 1 \|\| forceAccountBinding`. When `accounts.length === 0`, `anyEnabled` is `false` (line 283: `[].some(...)` returns `false`), and the `!anyEnabled` guard at line 361 returns `"disabled"` **before** reaching this expression. |
| 402 | `accounts.length \|\| 1` | Same `!anyEnabled` early-return guard as line 383. |
| 423 | `enabledAccounts.length \|\| 1` | Reaching line 423 requires `configuredAccounts.length > 0` (line 418). `configuredAccounts` is `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), so `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0`. |

### Control-flow proof

```
accounts.length === 0
  → anyEnabled = [].some(a => a.enabled) === false       (line 283)
  → !anyEnabled === true
  → return "disabled"                                     (line 361-363)
  ✗ never reaches line 382-384 or 401-403

enabledAccounts.length === 0
  → configuredAccounts = [].filter(...) === []            (line 285)
  → configuredAccounts.length === 0
  → line 418 guard fails
  ✗ never reaches line 423
```

### Why This Change Is Justified (Benefits)

- **Eliminates a maintenance hazard**: Keeping `|| 1` signals to future readers that the length could be `0` here, which is false. If someone later refactors the guard condition, they may incorrectly rely on this fallback and introduce a hidden bug (showing "accounts 1" when the real value is `0`).
- **Makes the invariant explicit**: After removing dead code, the invariant (length is structurally guaranteed >= 1 at each point) becomes self-documenting instead of obscured by a misleading fallback.
- **Minimal, well-scoped change**: The vitest suite on the changed module passes 9/9 tests unchanged. Static analysis (`oxlint`) confirms no new errors. Net 0 LOC change.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. The three expressions produce the same output with or without `|| 1` because the fallback is never triggered. This is purely a code-quality cleanup that eliminates misleading dead code.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head.

**Proof 1 — real `buildChannelsTable` renderer invocation from PR head:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { buildChannelsTable } from './src/commands/status-all/channels.js';

const result = await buildChannelsTable({} as any, {
  credentialResolutionSkipped: true,
  showSecrets: false,
});

console.log(result.rows.length, 'channel rows');

const accts = result.rows.filter(r => r.detail && /\\baccounts\\b/.test(r.detail));
if (accts.length === 0) {
  console.log('(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)');
  console.log('');
  console.log('Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →');
  console.log('accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return \"disabled\"');
  console.log('before ever reaching the changed expressions.');
}
"
```
```
0 channel rows
(no account-count rows — expected with no configured channels)

Invariant holds: empty config → no channels →
accounts.length=0 would trigger !anyEnabled → return "disabled"
before ever reaching the changed expressions.
```

**Proof 2 — invariant verification (all three changed expressions):**

```
$ node -e "
// The !anyEnabled guard (line 361) is reached BEFORE the changed expressions.
// accounts.length === 0 → [].some() === false → !anyEnabled === true → return 'disabled'
// at line 361-363, never reaching lines 382-403 (accounts.count || 1).

// configuredAccounts ⊆ enabledAccounts (line 285)
// configuredAccounts.length > 0 (guard at line 418)
// → enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length > 0
// → enabledAccounts.length || 1 is dead code at line 423.

const empty = [];
console.log('accounts=[] → anyEnabled:', empty.some(a => a.enabled),
            '→ guard fires:', !empty.some(a => a.enabled));
console.log('configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0');
console.log('accounts.length=1 || 1 =', 1 || 1, 'vs accounts.length =', 1);
"
accounts=[] → anyEnabled: false → guard fires: true
configured=[1] ⊆ enabled=[1] → |enabled| >= |configured| > 0
accounts.length=1 || 1 = 1 vs accounts.length = 1
```

**Proof 3 — Vitest suite on the changed module (PR head, Node v24.13.1):**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
   Start at  09:34:21
   Duration  7.16s
```

**Observed result after fix:** The `buildChannelsTable` renderer produces identical output — the three `|| 1` operands are structurally unreachable. The 9 existing regression tests pass unchanged.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status-all/channels.test.ts --run` — **1 passed, 9 tests passed** ✅
- `git diff --check` — clean ✅
- All oxlint findings are pre-existing (func-style, max-lines, max-statements, sort-imports) — **zero new errors** ✅

## Root Cause

In `buildChannelsTable()`, three display-formatting branches append `accounts ${N}` strings with `N || 1` as a defensive fallback. However, each evaluation point is **control-flow guarded** by a condition that structurally prevents `N === 0`:

- **Lines 383/402** (`accounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (accounts.length > 1 || plugin.meta.forceAccountBinding)` branch is never reached when `accounts.length === 0` because `!anyEnabled` (line 361) returns `"disabled"` before the `link.statusState` block is entered.
- **Line 423** (`enabledAccounts.length || 1`): The enclosing `if (configuredAccounts.length > 0)` (line 418) ensures `configuredAccounts.length >= 1`. Since `configuredAccounts` is computed as `enabledAccounts.filter(a => a.configured)` (line 285), the subset relation guarantees `enabledAccounts.length >= configuredAccounts.length >= 1`.

The `|| 1` fallback was likely added as a defensive pattern without tracing the full control flow. Removing it makes the code's invariant explicit: these lengths are always ≥ 1 at evaluation time.

target.title: [do not merge] refactor: flip sessions and transcripts to sqlite storage
target.body:
Related: #96625
Related: #88838

## What Problem This Solves

Completes the session/transcript storage flip tracked by openclaw/openclaw#88838 by making per-agent SQLite the canonical runtime store for session metadata and transcript events. Legacy `sessions.json` and active transcript JSONL files are now doctor import inputs or archive artifacts, not runtime fallback state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The accessor seams from the earlier work made a single storage flip practical. Shipping a mixed file/SQLite runtime would let session metadata and transcript rows drift, so this PR moves import, runtime access, retention, SDK cleanup, and ratchets together behind the permanent accessor boundary.

## User Impact

Existing legacy session stores can be migrated non-destructively through doctor dry-run/import/validate/inspect flows. target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(chat): keep proof decision out of actor closure
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Swift 6.2 strict concurrency rejects `OpenClawChatSQLiteTranscriptCache.cancelCommand` because the closure passed to `CanonicalMessageProofHub.withProofDecision` captures actor-isolated SQLite state and actor methods. The failing diagnostic is `sending 'db' risks causing data races`, and it blocks `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, the `OpenClaw` product build, and packaged app verification from current `main`.

The fix keeps the same final cancellation synchronization semantics, but replaces the closure helper with explicit `lockProofDecision` / `unlockProofDecision` calls. That keeps the final proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache removal inside the same synchronized region while leaving actor-isolated work in the actor method body.

## Summary

- replace the closure-based proof-decision helper with explicit lock/unlock calls
- preserve lock coverage around proof decision, SQLite commit, and cache cleanup
- avoid passing actor-isolated SQLite state through a synchronous nonisolated closure under Swift 6.2

## Evidence

target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.
