target.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock
target.body:
## Summary

A long-running gateway can permanently deadlock its entire agent lane on a stuck OAuth auth-refresh. The runtime auth single-flight in `auth-controller.ts` stores the in-flight refresh promise in `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight`; every model turn that needs auth does `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` **with no timeout**. If the underlying provider auth hook (`prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` -> OAuth refresh, keychain read, or cross-agent file-lock wait) never settles, `refreshInFlight` is never cleared and **every subsequent turn hangs forever** awaiting it. The process stays alive and the port stays open, so it looks healthy while no replies are produced.

Observed in production: a gateway froze mid-day right after a token hit expiry. Process alive (11d uptime, port listening) but fully idle since the freeze, zero sockets to the provider, all threads parked, one never-resolving `await`. On-disk token was valid the whole time (a fresh process pre-warmed auth in ~0.7s), and no on-disk lock was held — i.e. a pure in-memory single-flight deadlock.

This adds a hard deadline so the single-flight promise **always** settles:

- New `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline()` + `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (360s) in `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`. The worst legitimate case is two serialized in-lock budgets — waiting out a peer's full 150s critical section, then running our own 150s section — so 360s keeps 60s of real headroom above 300s; legitimate contention never misreports as a hard timeout while a true hang is forced to reject.
- `refreshRuntimeAuth` wraps the refresh operation in that deadline; on timeout it rejects, the `.finally` clears `refreshInFlight`, and all waiters unblock with a descriptive error instead of hanging.
- The `.finally` clear is no longer gated on `generation`: a profile rotation during a slow/hung refresh must still release the handle it owns, otherwise a stale handle wedges the new generation. The existing `refreshInFlight === refreshPromise` identity guard still prevents clobbering a newer refresh.

No behavior change on the happy path (fast refresh resolves long before the deadline). The deadline is a backstop only.

## Repro / Test plan

- [x] `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline` unit tests: rejects with the typed `RuntimeAuthDeadlineError` after the deadline when work never settles (fake timers), resolves/propagates when work wins the race, passes through unbounded for non-positive timeout, and the default exceeds two serialized in-lock budgets with explicit headroom.
- [x] `auth-controller` regression tests: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever sets `refreshInFlight`, then after advancing past the hard deadline the wedged handle rejects with `exceeded hard deadline` and is no longer the active in-flight handle; a deadline-abandoned refresh whose continuation later settles is discarded after a successful retry.
- [x] Proof the test catches the bug: with the deadline neutralized (timeout `0` = unbounded), the regression test **times out / FAILS**; restored, it passes.
- [x] Live repro harness (real timers, real 360s constant): deadline fires, lane recovers, stale completion discarded — full terminal capture in Evidence below.
- [x] Current-head scoped run: see Evidence below.

Thanks @amittell.

---

## Update: complete the deadlock class (not just the refresh path)

A follow-up audit found the original commit only backstopped ONE of several entry paths into the same auth lock/gate machinery. Both remaining paths could still permanently wedge the agent lane the same way:

1. **Cold-start / profile-rotation path (critical).** `applyApiKeyInfo` (the path `initializeAuthProfile` and `advanceAuthProfile` use, and the first turn a watchdog restart lands on) awaited `resolveApiKeyForCandidate` and `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` — the exact hook that hung in production — with no deadline. A single shared local `withAuthDeadline` helper now wraps every auth boundary in `auth-controller.ts` (refresh AND cold-start), so a hung provider hook fails the turn over instead of deadlocking the lane.
2. **In-lock keychain / buildApiKey (high).** In `oauth-manager.ts`, `withRefreshCallTimeout` wrapped only the network refresh call; the in-lock keychain store load and `buildApiKey` ran un-deadlined while the cross-agent file lock was held, so a wedged keychain pinned the lock and chain-stalled every same-key refresher behind the un-timed `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh gate (`refreshQueue.enqueue` chains each caller on the previous tail with no timeout). The whole held-lock critical section is now bounded by `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (150s), kept strictly between the 120s call timeout and the 180s stale window.

---

## Update 2: side-effect-safe timeouts (review findings)

The deadlines above abandon work they cannot cancel. The review correctly flagged that an abandoned continuation could later perform side effects while a successor owns the key. Head `08da7ebecf` closes both stale write-back paths and the budget arithmetic:

1. **In-lock OAuth write-back guard (`oauth-manager.ts`).** `withRefreshCallTimeout` now hands the critical section an ownership token (`{ state: "owned" | "abandoned" }`) that flips to `abandoned` the instant the section deadline fires — the same instant the file lock is released and a peer refresher can own the key. The continuation re-checks the token before **every** persist/mirror side effect (`adopt-bootstrap` write, refreshed-credential persist, main-store mirror) and no-ops with a debug log when stale, so it can never clobber a successor's freshly persisted tokens.
2. **Runtime auth generation invalidation (`auth-controller.ts` + `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`).** The deadline now rejects with a typed `RuntimeAuthDeadlineError`. When it abandons a refresh, the controller bumps `runtimeAuthState.generation`, so the abandoned completion — which snapshots generation/profile/source at entry — fails the existing stale-check and is discarded instead of overwriting the credentials a scheduled retry installed. Cold-start writes are sequenced strictly after their awaited deadline, so the abandoned cold-start work has no state write to guard beyond this.
3. **Outer budget headroom.** `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` raised 300s -> 360s. The previous value equaled exactly two serialized 150s in-lock budgets with zero headroom, so worst-case legitimate contention could misreport as a hard timeout. The invariant test now asserts `> 2 x OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS + 30s` (strict, explicit margin) instead of the old `>=` sum.

Regression tests added for both guards: `oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts` (real file locks and stores on disk; compressed budgets via the constants seam) and an `auth-controller` fake-timer test that proves a stale completion after deadline + retry cannot install its credentials.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` still awaits `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` in `auth-controller.ts` with no timeout, and the `.finally` clear is generation-gated, so one provider auth hook, keychain read, or cross-agent lock wait that never settles leaves the in-flight handle pending forever and every later model turn deadlocks awaiting it. The gateway process stays alive and its port stays open, so monitoring sees a healthy process while the agent lane produces no replies until a manual restart. This PR makes every runtime auth boundary settle — a hard 360s deadline on the single-flight refresh and cold-start paths, an ungated in-flight-handle clear, and a 150s bound on the whole held-lock OAuth critical section — and makes those deadlines side-effect-safe: abandoned continuations are ownership/generation-checked so they can never persist, mirror, or install credentials over a successor refresher.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` at d3ff48c51f. The only conflict this round was the import block of `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.ts` (main's #102009 egress-time credential injection vs this PR's deadline imports). Resolution keeps main's SecretRef egress guards exactly as shipped — `unwrapSecretSentinelsForProviderEgress` at the provider runtime-auth exchange, the `protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth` wrapper, and `secretSentinels: true` on `getApiKeyForModel` are byte-identical to `main` (the PR diff does not touch those lines) — and re-applies only the `withAuthDeadline` imports/wraps on top. The earlier `oauth-manager.ts` `KeyedAsyncQueue` resolution from the 22376d80e163 rebase is preserved unchanged.

Scoped test run at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts

 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

Sibling auth suites also pass at the same head (11 test files, 93 tests, 2 Vitest shards): `oauth-identity`, `oauth-lock-path`, `oauth-lock-timeout-classification`, `oauth-refresh-error`, `oauth-refresh-failure`, `oauth-refresh-queue`, `oauth-refresh-timeout`, `oauth-shared`, `oauth.adopt-identity`, `oauth.concurrent-agents`, `oauth.fallback-to-main-agent`, `oauth.mirror-refresh`, `oauth.openai-codex-refresh-fallback`, `oauth`, `effective-oauth`, `external-oauth`. `tsgo` core and core-test lanes exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all changed files.

### Live repro 1 — runtime auth deadline, lane recovery, stale discard (real timers, real 360s constant)

One-shot harness wiring a never-resolving `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` into the real `createEmbeddedRunAuthController`; nothing mocked but the provider seam, no fake timers, unmodified production constants. Captured terminal output:

```
[t+0.0s] RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS = 360000ms
[t+0.0s] provider auth hook call 1: initial exchange succeeds (expires in 60s)
[t+0.0s] setRuntimeApiKey(custom-openai, initial-runtime-key)
[t+0.0s] initializeAuthProfile complete; scheduled refresh due in ~5s (min delay)
[t+5.0s] [controller debug] Refreshing runtime auth for custom-openai (scheduled)...
[t+5.0s] provider auth hook call 2: scheduled refresh HANGS (never settles) — the wedge
[t+5.0s] refreshInFlight handle set; awaiting the REAL 360s hard deadline...
[t+365.0s] [controller debug] Invalidated runtime auth generation 1 for custom-openai; deadline abandoned an in-flight refresh.
[t+365.0s] [controller warn] Runtime auth refresh failed for custom-openai: Runtime auth operation for custom-openai exceeded hard deadline (360000ms)
[t+365.0s] DEADLINE FIRED: refreshInFlight rejected with: Runtime auth operation for custom-openai exceeded hard deadline (360000ms)
[t+365.0s] single-flight handle cleared — the lane is no longer wedged
[t+365.0s] waiting for the 60s scheduled-retry to install fresh credentials...
[t+425.0s] [controller debug] Refreshing runtime auth for custom-openai (scheduled-retry)...
[t+425.0s] provider auth hook call 3: retry resolves fresh credentials
[t+425.0s] setRuntimeApiKey(custom-openai, retry-runtime-key)
[t+425.0s] [controller debug] Runtime auth refreshed for custom-openai; expires in 3600s.
[t+425.1s] LANE RECOVERED: retry installed retry-runtime-key (next turn can proceed)
[t+425.1s] resolving the abandoned call-2 hook with STALE credentials now
[t+425.1s] [controller debug] Ignoring stale runtime auth refresh for custom-openai; auth state advanced before scheduled refresh completed.
[t+426.1s] STALE COMPLETION DISCARDED: installed keys = [initial-runtime-key, retry-runtime-key] (no stale-runtime-key)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed (1)
```

The deadline fires at the real 360s mark, the single-flight handle clears (lane un-wedged), the 60s scheduled retry installs fresh credentials (next turn proceeds), and the abandoned hook's eventual completion is discarded by the generation guard — `stale-runtime-key` is never installed.

### Live repro 2 — in-lock OAuth abandon, successor ownership, write-back discard (real file locks/stores)

Same-shape harness against the real `createOAuthManager` with the real cross-agent file lock and on-disk auth stores in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; only the two deadline budgets are compressed (1s / 10s) via the constants seam so the run is observable. Captured terminal output:

```
[t+0.05s] seeded sub-agent store with expired credential (access=expired-access)
[t+0.05s] turn 1: resolveOAuthAccess enters the global refresh lock and wedges
[t+0.06s] refresh call 1: token endpoint HANGS (in-lock deadline will abandon it)
[t+1.07s] IN-LOCK DEADLINE FIRED: turn 1 rejected with: OAuth token refresh failed for openai: OAuth refresh call "openai oauth refresh critical section" exceeded hard timeout (1000ms)
[t+1.07s] turn 2 (lane recovery): a new refresher takes the lock and succeeds
[t+1.08s] refresh call 2: successor refresher rotates tokens successfully
[t+1.09s] [auth-profiles debug] mirrored refreshed OAuth credential to main agent store {"profileId":"openai:oauth","expires":"2026-07-09T01:37:34.322Z"}
[t+1.10s] LANE RECOVERED: turn 2 resolved apiKey=successor-access
[t+1.10s] abandoned call-1 continuation now settles with STALE rotated tokens
[t+1.10s] [auth-profiles debug] discarded abandoned OAuth refresh write-back after in-lock deadline {"profileId":"openai:oauth","provider":"openai","step":"persist"}
[t+1.60s] STALE WRITE-BACK DISCARDED: sub store access=successor-access, main mirror access=successor-access (stale-abandoned-access absent)

The `discarded abandoned OAuth refresh write-back after in-lock deadline` line is the FIX 1 guard firing; the on-disk stores (sub + main mirror) retain the successor's tokens and the abandoned refresher's rotated tokens are never persisted.

Production soak on a fork: gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06, and the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: gateway agent lane permanently deadlocks when one runtime auth refresh never settles; every later model turn hangs on an un-timed `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` while the process looks healthy; additionally, deadline-abandoned refreshers could persist/mirror/install stale credentials over a successor refresher.
Real environment tested: live repro harnesses at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573 run with real timers and the unmodified 360s production constant (runtime path) and real cross-agent file locks plus on-disk auth stores (OAuth path); production gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run the deadline patch backported on a fork since 2026-06 with no recurrence of the freeze.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.abandoned-writeback.test.ts
Evidence after fix: 4 test files, 44 tests passed at head 08da7ebecf5a83a0d7f8049643d38c775e7e1573; 11 sibling oauth suites (93 tests) green at the same head; captured live-harness terminal output above shows the 360s deadline firing by wall clock, the lane recovering on the next scheduled retry, and both stale write-backs being discarded with the guard log lines.
Observed result after fix: a hung provider auth hook or in-lock keychain wait now rejects at the deadline, the in-flight handle is cleared, waiting turns fail over with a descriptive error instead of deadlocking, abandoned continuations no-op instead of persisting or installing stale credentials, and the production fork gateways have had no recurrence of the freeze.

target.title: fix(agent): treat Anthropic long-context usage errors as context overflow for compact+retry
target.body:
## Summary

Re-opening as new PR after #52030 was auto-closed by barnaclebot for the 10-PR cap; reviewers and Greptile evaluated the fix positively at the time and the underlying bug still applies on current main.

Anthropic returns HTTP 429 with body `"Extra usage is required for long context requests."` when a request hits the long-context usage tier. Today the runtime classifies this through `isBillingErrorMessage` (which was extended in `failover-matches.ts` to match `/extra usage is required(?: for long context requests)?/i`), short-circuiting before any context-overflow handling. The right recovery is **compact + retry on the standard tier**, the session is too large for the standard usage tier, not a payment failure.

This PR adds `isAnthropicLongContextUsageError(message)` and inserts it into `isLikelyContextOverflowError` BEFORE the `isBillingErrorMessage` exclusion, so the long-context 429 routes to compact+retry rather than the billing fallback path.

## Files

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`: new classifier + early-return inserted before the billing exclusion
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.ts`: re-export
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts`: coverage for the new classifier and the overflow short-circuit
- `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/help/faq-first-run.md`: document the compact+retry recovery path

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: An Anthropic HTTP 429 with body `Extra usage is required for long context requests.` is currently classified as a billing error by `isBillingErrorMessage` via the regex added in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.ts`. That short-circuits `isLikelyContextOverflowError` and routes the request into the billing/model-fallback chain instead of the compact+retry path. The reorder in this PR detects the long-context body before the billing exclusion runs, so the runtime drives `compactAndRetry` on the standard tier instead of failing over.
- Real environment tested: live deployed openclaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 71842, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Node v25.8.2, `/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw`. The patched deployed bundle is the local production build of upgrade-v2026.5.28 with PR #84972 layered on top, staged under `/tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/` on the same host as the running gateway; the deployed gateway dist at `/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/` is the same source tree without this PR and is used as the pre-fix baseline.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```
  ssh alexm@rh-bot.lan
  ls -la /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/.buildstamp
  # -> {"builtAt":...,"head":"23804e610c998a0532e0c90441b130b38e5e8cc8"}
  ps -p 71842 -o pid,etime,command
  grep -l "isAnthropicLongContextUsageError" /tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/*.js
  # -> /tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/errors-Br4OcmFZ.js
  node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell-baseline.mjs   # pre-patch baseline against live deployed bundle
  node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell.mjs            # post-patch behavior against patched deployed bundle
  ```
- Evidence after fix: realistic Anthropic error payloads exercised against the patched deployed bundle on rh-bot.lan. Output of `node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell.mjs`:
  ```
  --- direct isAnthropicLongContextUsageError checks ---
  PASS longContext.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: true
  PASS rateLimit.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  PASS promptTooLong.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  PASS unrelated.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  --- isLikelyContextOverflowError routing ---
  PASS longContext.isLikelyContextOverflowError: true
  PASS rateLimit.isLikelyContextOverflowError: false
  PASS promptTooLong.isLikelyContextOverflowError: true
  PASS unrelated.isLikelyContextOverflowError: false

  RESULT PASS (all checks)
  ```
  Output of `node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell-baseline.mjs` against the live deployed unpatched bundle on the same host:
  ```
  pre-patch isLikelyContextOverflowError(longContextMessage) = false
  BASELINE CONFIRMED: pre-patch deployed bundle misclassifies Anthropic long-context 429
  ```
- Observed result after fix: `isLikelyContextOverflowError("Extra usage is required for long context requests.")` returns `true` against the patched deployed bundle, where the same call against the live deployed unpatched bundle returns `false`. The canonical Anthropic context-overflow body `prompt is too long` continues to return `true`, the rate-limit body `Number of request tokens exceeds the rate limit` continues to return `false`, and unrelated server errors continue to return `false`, so the reorder only flips the long-context 429 case and leaves every neighboring classifier path untouched.
- What was not tested: end-to-end observation of an Anthropic 429 with the long-context body actually arriving at the deployed gateway and driving `compactAndRetry` through to a successful retry. Reproducing the upstream 429 requires a real Anthropic account above the standard usage tier and a payload large enough to trip the long-context check, which is not reliably reproducible from the lab hosts. The classifier surface that decides the routing has been exercised directly against the patched deployed bundle, and the equivalent in-tree unit suites under `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/` pass locally.

## Refs

- Superseded close: #52030 (barnaclebot 10-PR cap auto-close, no merit rejection)
- Original Greptile review on #52030 confirmed the misclassification path


## Post-rebase verification (2026-07-08, head df072e54b6)

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (d3ff48c51f), conflict-free; none of the intervening commits touch this PR's files or the overflow-recovery harness. The earlier docs conflict resolution (previous rebase onto 22376d80e1) is preserved: `docs/help/faq-first-run.md` re-applies the compact+retry sentence onto main's condensed accordion shape, and `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md` was trimmed so the fallback-model step no longer implies configured fallback models engage after exhausted compaction, matching the `model-fallback.ts` contract that rethrows context-overflow errors instead of failing over.

### Fixture proof: full runner path with the real classifier

New runner-level test in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts`, extending the existing overflow-compaction harness:

> `overflow compaction in run loop > routes the Anthropic long-context 429 through compaction and terminates blocked without model fallback`

The harness's default `mockedIsLikelyContextOverflowError` is a reimplementation that only matches `request_too_large`-style bodies, so the test swaps in the real classifiers via `vi.importActual("../embedded-agent-helpers/errors.js")` and feeds a synthetic Anthropic 429 carrying the exact body `"Extra usage is required for long context requests."` through `runEmbeddedAgent`. It proves, end to end inside the embedded runner:

- the body still matches `isBillingErrorMessage` (asserted as a sanity check); only this PR's early return inside `isLikelyContextOverflowError` reroutes it, so it is classified as context overflow, not billing or rate limit;
- compaction is attempted: 3 compact+retry cycles, 4 attempts total;
- every retry stays on the original `anthropic/test-model` with `fallbackActive: false`; no fallback model is ever selected, matching the `model-fallback.ts:1789-1796` contract that rethrows context-overflow errors so the runner's compaction owns them;
- after exhausted compaction the run terminates with the canonical blocked result: `meta.error.kind === "context_overflow"`, `meta.livenessState === "blocked"`, and an error payload with the standard reset/new guidance.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  149 passed (149)
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 34.56s
```

Note on the terminal state: terminating blocked after exhausted compaction (instead of engaging configured fallback models) is the pre-existing `main` contract for ALL context-overflow errors, asserted by the pre-existing exhaustion cases in `run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts` (`context_overflow` / `compaction_failure` kinds) and enforced by the deliberate context-overflow rethrow in `model-fallback.ts`. This PR only makes the Anthropic long-context 429 join that existing contract; the exhausted-overflow terminal-state redesign is tracked separately in #9986. Explicitly decided: status quo here.

The classifier suite at the new head still includes main's newer tests asserting the exact long-context body continues to classify as billing via `isBillingErrorMessage` / `classifyFailoverReason` (this PR only reorders `isLikelyContextOverflowError` and leaves those classifiers untouched). Lint (`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`) and `oxfmt --check` on the touched TS files are clean.

target.title: fix(telegram): silently skip empty-text sends
target.body:
Supersedes #59725 (auto-closed by the 10-open-PR cap; not reopenable because the close `stateReason` is `COMPLETED` and the branch was force-pushed since). ## Scope note: re-derived on top of current main Most of the original branch scope has since landed on `main` through other work, so this PR was reset onto `main` and re-implemented to cover only the residual gaps: - #56620 added `filterEmptyTelegramTextChunks` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`), which already drops whitespace-only chunks before any send. - The `sendTelegramText` rewrite around `sendPlainFallback` / `buildTelegramPlainFallbackPlan` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`) already recovers formatted-send failures when a non-empty plain fallback exists. - #93279 introduced the default-vs-rich delivery split, which this PR preserves: the rich lane stays opt-in behind `richMessages === true` and both lanes get the same skip semantics. Two gaps remain on current `main`, and they are exactly the reported user path: 1. `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` only matches Telegram's legacy `message text is empty` wording. The live Bot API now also returns `text must be non-empty` (raw round-trip below), so the empty-text 400 escapes the recovery branch. 2. When non-whitespace source renders to empty visible text and the plain fallback is also empty (for example `` with `plainText: ""`), `main` throws (`empty rich text and empty plain fallback` / `empty formatted text and empty plain fallback`) or rethrows the 400 from the catch block, surfacing a user-visible delivery failure for content the model never made visible. ## Behavior addressed Interrupted mid-reply turns can produce formatted Telegram HTML that has no visible text and no plain-text fallback, for example an empty supported tag such as ``. Telegram rejects that payload with HTTP 400 (`message text is empty` legacy wording, `text must be non-empty` newer wording). Previously this surfaced as a user-visible delivery failure; this PR silently treats that empty-text send as a no-op with correct accounting. Parse errors remain out of scope and still throw (bare `
` payloads fail as parse errors, per the live baseline below). ## Change - `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` now also matches `text must be non-empty` and the rich-lane `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` rejection. - `sendTelegramText` returns `Promise`: when the rendered payload is empty and the plain fallback is also empty, it resolves `undefined` (silent no-op) instead of throwing, both pre-flight and when Telegram rejects the payload as empty. Sends with a usable plain fallback still recover exactly as on `main`; parse errors and unrelated failures still throw. - `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` treats an `undefined` chunk result as a no-op: no `markReplyApplied`, no `markDelivered`, so skipped chunks do not advance reply state, delivered count, transcript mirroring, `message_sent.success`, or pinning. - Review fix (clawsweeper finding on the previous revision): in the suppressed single-use multi-chunk lane (the Telegram Desktop workaround in `reply-threading.ts`), the reply target is now consumed on the first delivered chunk instead of being keyed to chunk index 0. Previously a silently-skipped chunk 0 left `progress.hasReplied` false forever, leaking unconsumed single-use reply state to later sends in the same batch that share the delivery progress (`deliverReplies` creates one shared progress per batch). `markReplyApplied` is idempotent, so delivered chunks after the first are no-ops. - Voice fallback text paths mirror only text that actually reached Telegram: an all-skipped caption fallback no longer registers `reply.text` as delivered transcript content. ## Verification Run after this patch on the rebased head (current `main` d3ff48c51f + this commit): ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts -> 4 files, 83 tests passed node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram -> 134 files, 2464 tests passed (the pre-rebase bot.test.ts failure noted in the previous revision no longer reproduces on current main) node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json -> clean node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json -> clean oxlint -> clean oxfmt --check -> clean ``` The new regression test (`reply-threading.test.ts`, skipped chunk 0 followed by two delivered chunks) fails on the previous revision with `expected [ false, false, false ] to deeply equal [ false, false, true ]` and passes with the fix; a second case pins that across separate single-chunk sends sharing progress, the reply target attaches to the first delivered send exactly once and skipped sends neither consume nor break the chain. ## Live Telegram round-trip Raw Telegram Bot API baseline (no OpenClaw code), re-run 2026-07-08 against the live Bot API: ``` payload="
" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unsupported start tag \"br\" at byte offset 0" payload="" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: text must be non-empty" payload="OpenClaw PR 88810 raw Bot API baseline: delivered reply" -> ok=true message_id=11323 ``` `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText`, run on the exact rebased head `f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd` against the live Bot API (token and chat id redacted): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) (a) empty html + empty plain fallback -> resolved: undefined [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11324 (b) normal payload -> resolved message_id: 11324 ``` Second `tsx` driver on the same exact head exercising the fixed `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` single-use consumption lane live (chunk 0 renders empty and is skipped by Telegram, chunk 1 delivers, then a follow-up send shares the same delivery progress): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11325 anchor message_id: 11325 [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11326 multi-chunk batch: sendChunk replyToMessageId per chunk: [ undefined, undefined ] progress.hasReplied after skipped chunk 0 + delivered chunk 1: true [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11327 follow-up sendChunk replyToMessageId: [ undefined ] ``` The suppressed multi-chunk lane attaches the native reply param to no chunk by design (Telegram Desktop workaround); the state proof is `progress.hasReplied: true` after the first delivered chunk and the follow-up send not resurrecting the anchor reply target. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Empty visible-text Telegram HTML sends with an empty plain fallback no longer surface as delivery failures; they are treated as no-op sends with no phantom delivery accounting and no leaked single-use reply state, while parse errors and fallback-capable sends behave as on main. Real environment tested: Live Telegram Bot API on the exact rebased head f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd (raw `sendMessage` curl baseline plus a `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText` via grammY), and local Vitest runs of the rebased code. Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram`, and the live driver above on the exact head. Evidence after fix: 83/83 tests pass across the four delivery/reply test files, including the new consumption regression (skipped chunk 0 no longer strands `progress.hasReplied`); live Bot API on the exact head resolves `undefined` for `` with `plainText: ""` (logged as a skip, no throw) and returns a real `message_id` (11324) for a normal payload. Observed result after fix: Empty-text sends skip silently without advancing reply delivery state; the single-use reply target is consumed by the first delivered chunk even when earlier chunks skip; payloads with real content or a usable plain fallback deliver unchanged; bare `
` HTML still throws the Telegram parse error and remains out of scope. What was not tested: No full live interrupted-agent session was exercised; the live driver exercises `sendTelegramText` directly rather than the whole `deliverReplies` pipeline over a running gateway. Focused regression tests cover send skipping, reply accounting, single-use reply consumption, transcript mirroring, hooks, pin behavior, and voice fallback paths.

target.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
target.body:
## Summary

Grounds assistant transcript text before session-context replay: an absolute path under the managed media dir that does not resolve to a real file is redacted to `[unverified media reference removed]`, keeping the surrounding prose. User text is never rewritten, and paths outside the managed media dir (code paths, host paths) are exempt so ordinary technical conversation is untouched.

Motivation is a live incident on a production gateway (2026-07-06): a bare 3-character inbound message ("Hey", no attachment, WhatsApp plugin disabled) produced an assistant turn containing `IMAGE:<media-dir>/whats-app-image-2026-07-06-...jpg` plus a detailed description of an image that never existed on disk or in the gateway inbound log. The session-context replay then compiled that fabricated text into every subsequent prompt (`context.compiled` / `prompt.submitted` in the trajectory), making the hallucination self-reinforcing for the rest of the session.

The invariant this leans on: legitimate inbound media never reaches prompts as a raw absolute path -- `media-note.ts` normalizes managed refs to `media://inbound/...`. So a raw absolute managed-media path inside *assistant* text is either fabricated or expired; both are unusable and safe to redact. This deliberately does not attempt free-text hallucination detection -- it only removes verifiably ungrounded media references, deterministically, with zero model calls.

Implementation: `redactUngroundedMediaRefs` in `src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.ts`, wired into `parseRecentConversationText` (assistant branch only) in `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, which serves `readRecentUserAssistantTextForSession` and its plugin-sdk consumers (e.g. the Telegram session transcript context). Handles the macOS `/private/var` twin, path-token boundaries (no substring matches inside longer paths or words), and trailing sentence punctuation; returns the same reference on no-op.

## Verification

- New colocated tests: 8 unit cases (fabricated ref redacted with prose kept, verified ref preserved, non-media absolute paths untouched, `/private` twin, token boundaries, trailing punctuation, mixed refs, no-op identity) plus a reader-level regression that replays the observed incident shape through `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` against real files in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (fabricated ref redacted; real-file ref and user text preserved verbatim).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`: 61 passed / 0 failed on this branch (includes the pre-existing 51 transcript reader tests, unchanged).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on touched files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: A hallucinated managed-media path in an assistant turn (fabricated `IMAGE:<media-dir>/...jpg` reference to a file that never existed) was replayed verbatim into subsequent prompt context, reinforcing the fabrication across the session.
Real environment tested: macOS 26 source checkout; reader-level regression executes the real transcript reader against a real on-disk session transcript and real files under a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media dir (no mocks in the replay path); incident evidence from a production macOS gateway trajectory (session ab2e822c, 2026-07-06 09:21 EDT).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: assistant entry text returned by `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` is `IMAGE:[unverified media reference removed] That's a serious setup. Original at <real file>.` -- the fabricated path is gone, the verified real-file ref and all prose survive, and the user entry containing the same fake path is returned unmodified.
Observed result after fix: 61 passed / 0 failed.
What was not tested: a live gateway restart/deploy with the incident session replayed end-to-end over Telegram; the fix is currently soaking on a fork deployment branch before fleet rollout.

target.title: fix: retry signal session-init conflicts
target.body:
## Summary
- retry Signal debounce flushes when reply session initialization conflicts with a just-finished turn
- bound the retry loop with short backoff delays and keep non-conflict failures unchanged
- add a focused regression test for the conflict-then-success path plus adjacent Signal coverage

## What Problem This Solves
A follow-up Signal DM that arrives right after the previous reply turn can hit `reply session initialization conflicted` during the debounce flush path and get dropped after a single logged failure. This patch adds a small bounded retry with backoff so the next flush attempt can reuse the just-finished session state instead of silently losing the message.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(agent): treat Anthropic long-context usage errors as context overflow for compact+retry
target.body:
## Summary

Re-opening as new PR after #52030 was auto-closed by barnaclebot for the 10-PR cap; reviewers and Greptile evaluated the fix positively at the time and the underlying bug still applies on current main.

Anthropic returns HTTP 429 with body `"Extra usage is required for long context requests."` when a request hits the long-context usage tier. Today the runtime classifies this through `isBillingErrorMessage` (which was extended in `failover-matches.ts` to match `/extra usage is required(?: for long context requests)?/i`), short-circuiting before any context-overflow handling. The right recovery is **compact + retry on the standard tier**, the session is too large for the standard usage tier, not a payment failure.

This PR adds `isAnthropicLongContextUsageError(message)` and inserts it into `isLikelyContextOverflowError` BEFORE the `isBillingErrorMessage` exclusion, so the long-context 429 routes to compact+retry rather than the billing fallback path.

## Files

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts`: new classifier + early-return inserted before the billing exclusion
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.ts`: re-export
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts`: coverage for the new classifier and the overflow short-circuit
- `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md`, `docs/help/faq-first-run.md`: document the compact+retry recovery path

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: An Anthropic HTTP 429 with body `Extra usage is required for long context requests.` is currently classified as a billing error by `isBillingErrorMessage` via the regex added in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.ts`. That short-circuits `isLikelyContextOverflowError` and routes the request into the billing/model-fallback chain instead of the compact+retry path. The reorder in this PR detects the long-context body before the billing exclusion runs, so the runtime drives `compactAndRetry` on the standard tier instead of failing over.
- Real environment tested: live deployed openclaw gateway on rh-bot.lan, pid 71842, build SHA 23804e610c (upgrade-v2026.5.28 with this PR cherry-picked). macOS Darwin 25.5.0, Node v25.8.2, `/opt/homebrew/bin/openclaw`. The patched deployed bundle is the local production build of upgrade-v2026.5.28 with PR #84972 layered on top, staged under `/tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/` on the same host as the running gateway; the deployed gateway dist at `/Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/` is the same source tree without this PR and is used as the pre-fix baseline.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```
  ssh alexm@rh-bot.lan
  ls -la /Users/alexm/.openclaw/openclaw/dist/.buildstamp
  # -> {"builtAt":...,"head":"23804e610c998a0532e0c90441b130b38e5e8cc8"}
  ps -p 71842 -o pid,etime,command
  grep -l "isAnthropicLongContextUsageError" /tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/*.js
  # -> /tmp/openclaw-pr-84972/dist/errors-Br4OcmFZ.js
  node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell-baseline.mjs   # pre-patch baseline against live deployed bundle
  node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell.mjs            # post-patch behavior against patched deployed bundle
  ```
- Evidence after fix: realistic Anthropic error payloads exercised against the patched deployed bundle on rh-bot.lan. Output of `node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell.mjs`:
  ```
  --- direct isAnthropicLongContextUsageError checks ---
  PASS longContext.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: true
  PASS rateLimit.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  PASS promptTooLong.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  PASS unrelated.isAnthropicLongContextUsageError: false
  --- isLikelyContextOverflowError routing ---
  PASS longContext.isLikelyContextOverflowError: true
  PASS rateLimit.isLikelyContextOverflowError: false
  PASS promptTooLong.isLikelyContextOverflowError: true
  PASS unrelated.isLikelyContextOverflowError: false

  RESULT PASS (all checks)
  ```
  Output of `node /tmp/proof-84972-amittell-baseline.mjs` against the live deployed unpatched bundle on the same host:
  ```
  pre-patch isLikelyContextOverflowError(longContextMessage) = false
  BASELINE CONFIRMED: pre-patch deployed bundle misclassifies Anthropic long-context 429
  ```
- Observed result after fix: `isLikelyContextOverflowError("Extra usage is required for long context requests.")` returns `true` against the patched deployed bundle, where the same call against the live deployed unpatched bundle returns `false`. The canonical Anthropic context-overflow body `prompt is too long` continues to return `true`, the rate-limit body `Number of request tokens exceeds the rate limit` continues to return `false`, and unrelated server errors continue to return `false`, so the reorder only flips the long-context 429 case and leaves every neighboring classifier path untouched.
- What was not tested: end-to-end observation of an Anthropic 429 with the long-context body actually arriving at the deployed gateway and driving `compactAndRetry` through to a successful retry. Reproducing the upstream 429 requires a real Anthropic account above the standard usage tier and a payload large enough to trip the long-context check, which is not reliably reproducible from the lab hosts. The classifier surface that decides the routing has been exercised directly against the patched deployed bundle, and the equivalent in-tree unit suites under `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/` pass locally.

## Refs

- Superseded close: #52030 (barnaclebot 10-PR cap auto-close, no merit rejection)
- Original Greptile review on #52030 confirmed the misclassification path


## Post-rebase verification (2026-07-08, head df072e54b6)

Rebased onto current `upstream/main` (d3ff48c51f), conflict-free; none of the intervening commits touch this PR's files or the overflow-recovery harness. The earlier docs conflict resolution (previous rebase onto 22376d80e1) is preserved: `docs/help/faq-first-run.md` re-applies the compact+retry sentence onto main's condensed accordion shape, and `docs/gateway/troubleshooting.md` was trimmed so the fallback-model step no longer implies configured fallback models engage after exhausted compaction, matching the `model-fallback.ts` contract that rethrows context-overflow errors instead of failing over.

### Fixture proof: full runner path with the real classifier

New runner-level test in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts`, extending the existing overflow-compaction harness:

> `overflow compaction in run loop > routes the Anthropic long-context 429 through compaction and terminates blocked without model fallback`

The harness's default `mockedIsLikelyContextOverflowError` is a reimplementation that only matches `request_too_large`-style bodies, so the test swaps in the real classifiers via `vi.importActual("../embedded-agent-helpers/errors.js")` and feeds a synthetic Anthropic 429 carrying the exact body `"Extra usage is required for long context requests."` through `runEmbeddedAgent`. It proves, end to end inside the embedded runner:

- the body still matches `isBillingErrorMessage` (asserted as a sanity check); only this PR's early return inside `isLikelyContextOverflowError` reroutes it, so it is classified as context overflow, not billing or rate limit;
- compaction is attempted: 3 compact+retry cycles, 4 attempts total;
- every retry stays on the original `anthropic/test-model` with `fallbackActive: false`; no fallback model is ever selected, matching the `model-fallback.ts:1789-1796` contract that rethrows context-overflow errors so the runner's compaction owns them;
- after exhausted compaction the run terminates with the canonical blocked result: `meta.error.kind === "context_overflow"`, `meta.livenessState === "blocked"`, and an error payload with the standard reset/new guidance.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts

      Tests  149 passed (149)
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 34.56s
```

Note on the terminal state: terminating blocked after exhausted compaction (instead of engaging configured fallback models) is the pre-existing `main` contract for ALL context-overflow errors, asserted by the pre-existing exhaustion cases in `run.overflow-compaction.loop.test.ts` (`context_overflow` / `compaction_failure` kinds) and enforced by the deliberate context-overflow rethrow in `model-fallback.ts`. This PR only makes the Anthropic long-context 429 join that existing contract; the exhausted-overflow terminal-state redesign is tracked separately in #9986. Explicitly decided: status quo here.

The classifier suite at the new head still includes main's newer tests asserting the exact long-context body continues to classify as billing via `isBillingErrorMessage` / `classifyFailoverReason` (this PR only reorders `isLikelyContextOverflowError` and leaves those classifiers untouched). target.title: fix(sessions): ground assistant transcript media refs before replay
target.body:
## Summary

Grounds assistant transcript text before session-context replay: an absolute path under the managed media dir that does not resolve to a real file is redacted to `[unverified media reference removed]`, keeping the surrounding prose. User text is never rewritten, and paths outside the managed media dir (code paths, host paths) are exempt so ordinary technical conversation is untouched.

Motivation is a live incident on a production gateway (2026-07-06): a bare 3-character inbound message ("Hey", no attachment, WhatsApp plugin disabled) produced an assistant turn containing `IMAGE:<media-dir>/whats-app-image-2026-07-06-...jpg` plus a detailed description of an image that never existed on disk or in the gateway inbound log. The session-context replay then compiled that fabricated text into every subsequent prompt (`context.compiled` / `prompt.submitted` in the trajectory), making the hallucination self-reinforcing for the rest of the session.

The invariant this leans on: legitimate inbound media never reaches prompts as a raw absolute path -- `media-note.ts` normalizes managed refs to `media://inbound/...`. So a raw absolute managed-media path inside *assistant* text is either fabricated or expired; both are unusable and safe to redact. This deliberately does not attempt free-text hallucination detection -- it only removes verifiably ungrounded media references, deterministically, with zero model calls.

Implementation: `redactUngroundedMediaRefs` in `src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.ts`, wired into `parseRecentConversationText` (assistant branch only) in `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, which serves `readRecentUserAssistantTextForSession` and its plugin-sdk consumers (e.g. the Telegram session transcript context). Handles the macOS `/private/var` twin, path-token boundaries (no substring matches inside longer paths or words), and trailing sentence punctuation; returns the same reference on no-op.

## Verification

- New colocated tests: 8 unit cases (fabricated ref redacted with prose kept, verified ref preserved, non-media absolute paths untouched, `/private` twin, token boundaries, trailing punctuation, mixed refs, no-op identity) plus a reader-level regression that replays the observed incident shape through `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` against real files in a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (fabricated ref redacted; real-file ref and user text preserved verbatim).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`: 61 passed / 0 failed on this branch (includes the pre-existing 51 transcript reader tests, unchanged).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` clean on touched files.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: A hallucinated managed-media path in an assistant turn (fabricated `IMAGE:<media-dir>/...jpg` reference to a file that never existed) was replayed verbatim into subsequent prompt context, reinforcing the fabrication across the session.
Real environment tested: macOS 26 source checkout; reader-level regression executes the real transcript reader against a real on-disk session transcript and real files under a temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` media dir (no mocks in the replay path); incident evidence from a production macOS gateway trajectory (session ab2e822c, 2026-07-06 09:21 EDT).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/transcript-grounding.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: assistant entry text returned by `readRecentUserAssistantTextFromSessionTranscript` is `IMAGE:[unverified media reference removed] That's a serious setup. Original at <real file>.` -- the fabricated path is gone, the verified real-file ref and all prose survive, and the user entry containing the same fake path is returned unmodified.
Observed result after fix: 61 passed / 0 failed.
What was not tested: a live gateway restart/deploy with the incident session replayed end-to-end over Telegram; the fix is currently soaking on a fork deployment branch before fleet rollout.

target.title: fix: inject completion acknowledgment when tool-only turns produce no text
target.body:
## Summary

When a model turn consists entirely of tool calls (file edits, memory writes, exec commands) with zero visible text in the response, the user sees nothing delivered to Telegram. The operations complete successfully but no message appears in the chat.

## Root Cause

In `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`, when `payloadArray.length === 0`, the code returns `undefined` unconditionally — even when tool calls were successfully executed. This makes the turn invisible to the user.

## Fix

Added a check for `runResult.meta?.toolSummary?.calls > 0` before returning. When tools ran but produced no text payload, a short `"Done."` acknowledgment is injected so the user knows the work completed.

## Testing

- The change is a 6-line addition in a single location
- The fix follows the existing code pattern (`returnWithQueuedFollowupDrain({ text: "..." })`)
- No behavior change when no tools ran (still returns `undefined` as before)
- No behavior change when payloads were produced (skips the empty check entirely)

Closes #79472

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

**After-fix live proof (patched build, live end-to-end gateway; plus stock 2026.6.11 A/B).** Captured 2026-07-08 on a scratch, isolated gateway (disposable VM, loopback-only bind, token auth, live Anthropic model) driving the real WebChat reply path via the documented gateway-client WS handshake and `chat.send`. Identical harness and trigger on both builds. Session identifiers are synthetic (`pr101920-live`); hosts/IPs/paths redacted.

*Trigger (real code path, no mocks):* seed `sessions.json` with a wedge-shaped entry so reply-session init adopts sessionId `pr101920-live-wedged`; start a long-running **hold** exec turn as a real in-flight admission of that identity; an external **toucher** process continuously rewrites the entry's `sessionFile` (atomic tmp+rename) so the **probe** turn's init snapshot→commit revision guard keeps losing the optimistic-concurrency race; the toucher stops once the self-heal marker appears so the post-heal retry can commit. Calibration honesty: fixed-cadence bumps (8ms, then 1ms) produced **0** conflicts — the snapshot→commit window is sub-millisecond; only continuous spin-writes reproduce the repeated-conflict wedge live. Non-triggering calibration runs are preserved alongside the golden artifacts.

*Patched build (PR head `09aac6a`) — self-heal fires, fenced drain works, turn completes with real tool output:*

```
# double conflict -> fenced self-heal requested (2 warn events)
2026-07-08T23:30:53.787+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry
2026-07-08T23:30:53.798+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry

# the in-flight foreign hold turn (admitted 23:30:44.36) is drained via the fence, not torn down mid-lock
message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-hold-20260708T233043Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=completed duration=9432ms reason=reply_operation_aborted
```

Probe turn final WS frame at 23:31:20.17 — `"state":"final","stopReason":"stop"`, and the healed session's reply body carries the actual `exec` output:

```
The exact tool output is:

PR101920_REAL_TOOL_OUTPUT_NONEMPTY
```

Whole patched run: **0 `outcome=error` events** and **0** `Error: reply session initialization conflicted` throws in the gateway log. The final committed session store (`sessions.final.json`) contains the previously-uncommittable entry for the wedged sessionKey — the healed init retry committed it (with the toucher's last `sessionFile` write), which is exactly what the pre-fix wedge could never do.

*Stock `openclaw@2026.6.11` (npm) — same trigger, user-visible hard failure:*

```
2026-07-08T23:35:59.292+00:00 [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=webchat sessionId=unknown sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live source=replyResolver outcome=error duration=17ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
2026-07-08T23:35:59.296+00:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-probe-20260708T233503Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=error duration=51444ms error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"
```

WS client terminal frame — the assistant's final message body **is** the conflict error, and no assistant delta/final frame ever carried the tool output:

```
"state":"error","errorMessage":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live","message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live"}]}
```

Stock contains no self-heal marker (0 occurrences) and the toucher ran to its timeout (no marker to stop on).

*Stored-state compatibility observed live:* both builds ran against identically seeded `sessions.json` files in the current 2026.6.11 shape; the patched build read and committed that store with no schema change — `sessions.final.json` is a standard sessions map (same fields, no new/renamed keys).

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.

target.title: improve(ui/usage): guard against usageResult missing its sessions array
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the **Usage** page, `UsagePage.render()` computes `sessionsLimitReached` from `this.usageResult?.sessions.length`. The optional chain guards `usageResult` but not its `sessions` field, so if `usageResult` is a truthy object without a populated `sessions` array, the render throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')` and the Usage page fails to render.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling line directly above already defends the same field with a guard:

```ts
sessions: this.usageResult?.sessions ?? [],
sessionsLimitReached: (this.usageResult?.sessions.length ?? 0) >= 1000,  // missing the second ?.
```

This change adds the missing `?.` so the two lines are consistent. It is defensive hardening; behavior is unchanged for well-formed data (where `sessions` is always present).

## User Impact

The Usage page no longer risks an uncaught render crash if it ever receives a `usageResult` object without a `sessions` array. No change for normal, well-formed responses.

## Evidence

- **Scope, stated honestly:** I found this by pointing an automated QA agent at the Control UI via the repo's `dev:ui:mock` server, where the `sessions.usage` request is unimplemented and falls through to `{}` (a non-null object with no `sessions`), which triggers the crash on `/usage`. I then traced the real gateway handler (`src/gateway/server-methods/usage.ts`): its single success path always returns `result.sessions` as an array, and every error branch is caught by the UI and sets `usageResult = null` (safe). I did **not** find a shipped path where the real gateway returns `ok: true` with a sessionless object. So I am filing this as defensive hardening consistent with the existing guard on the line above, **not** as a confirmed real-gateway crash.
- **Reproduction (LLM-free, Playwright):** against `dev:ui:mock`, a standalone repro navigating to `/usage` exits 0 (page-error reproduces) on `main` and exits 1 (no page-error) with this change. Before/after: the page went from a blank crashed render (uncaught `TypeError`) to rendering with zero page errors.

## AI Assistance

🤖 This change was found and prepared with AI assistance (an automated QA agent for discovery and deterministic reproduction). I have reviewed the one-line change and understand what it does. I attempted `codex review --base origin/main` locally; it did not complete within my time budget, so I am relying on the diff's simplicity and the reproduction evidence above.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Verified in a clean temporary worktree on branch `fix/subagent-target-alsoallow-tools`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression test covers `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.

target.title: fix(doctor): migrate legacy google provider config to current catalog schema (#102138)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138. On upgrade, a `models.providers.google` block generated by an
older OpenClaw version passes the persisted **config** schema but fails the
stricter **model-catalog** schema. The whole provider is silently dropped — all
`google/*` models become "not allowed" — and any fallback chain that selects a
gemini model then hangs for 120s on the LLM idle watchdog.

Three schema divergences (confirmed at current `main`):

1. **Missing provider `api`** — catalog validation throws `no "api" specified`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:505`).
2. **`input` enum tightened** to `("text"|"image")[]`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:165`); legacy blocks store
   `["text","image","audio","video"]`.
3. **`cost.cacheWrite` now required** (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:166`);
   legacy `cost` omits it.

The persisted config schema (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:382`) still accepts
`audio`/`video` and keeps `cacheWrite` optional, so an old block parses fine
then breaks at catalog load — a schema tightening with no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair lives in the **Google plugin doctor contract**
(`extensions/google/`), not core. The doctor contract registry already collects
plugin ids from `models.providers` keys
(`src/plugins/doctor-contract-registry.ts:261`) and applies each plugin's
`normalizeCompatibilityConfig`, so a `models.providers.google` block runs the
Google repair without hardcoding google ids or API defaults in the core
migration registry. This follows the established `extensions/ollama` /
`extensions/google-meet` config-compat pattern and keeps provider-owned config
policy in the provider plugin (AGENTS.md:31).

`extensions/google/src/config-compat.ts` (new), for `google`/`google-vertex`
blocks under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`:

- backfills provider-level `api` (`google` → `google-generative-ai`,
  `google-vertex` → `google-vertex`) — never overwrites a user-set `api`;
- narrows each model's `input` to `["text","image"]`;
- backfills `cost.cacheWrite: 0` when a `cost` object omits it.

Detection and repair share one `providerNeedsApiBackfill` predicate (provider
has no api **and** at least one model has no api → set provider api). A mixed
block — provider no api, one model with api, one without — is therefore fully
repaired and re-detection returns false, fixing the idempotency gap where the
previous asymmetric guard left the api-less model still invalid at catalog
load. Preserves SecretRef `apiKey` / `baseUrl`; leaves non-google providers
untouched.

## Addressing the prior review

- **[P1] Keep Google repair in the plugin doctor contract** — done: moved out
  of `legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.ts` into the Google plugin
  doctor contract; those core files are now byte-identical to `main`.
- **[P2] Repair mixed model API entries idempotently** — done: shared predicate
  (see above); covered by a dedicated test and the end-to-end proof.

## Evidence

### Focused tests — 10/10 (`extensions/google/src/config-compat.test.ts`)

```
✓ detects a legacy google block
✓ backfills api, narrows input, and fills cost.cacheWrite
✓ preserves the secret-ref apiKey and baseUrl
✓ is idempotent: re-running the migrated config reports no changes
✓ uses the google-vertex api for the google-vertex provider
✓ repairs a mixed model-api block so no model is left without an api (idempotent)
✓ does not overwrite a user-set provider api
✓ leaves models without a cost object untouched
✓ does not touch non-google providers
✓ handles non-record model entries without throwing
```

Core regression (`legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.test.ts`): 10/10
still pass after removing the core migration.

### End-to-end proof — real plugin doctor-contract path + real ModelRegistry

Part A ran the issue's verbatim legacy block through the real plugin
compatibility entry point (`applyPluginDoctorCompatibilityMigrations` →
`resolvePluginDoctorContracts` → the Google doctor contract), proving the
migration is discovered and applied via the plugin seam:

```
CHANGES (from the google plugin doctor contract):
  - Narrowed models.providers.google.models[0].input to ["text","image"]
  - Set models.providers.google.models[0].cost.cacheWrite to 0
  - Set models.providers.google.api to "google-generative-ai"
```

Part B loaded the block through the real `ModelRegistry` before/after:

```
BEFORE → getError():
   Invalid models.json schema:
     - providers.google.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.input.3: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.cost.cacheWrite: must have required properties cacheWrite
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') === undefined  (silently dropped)
AFTER  → getError(): (none)
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') → gemini-2.5-pro, input ["text","image"]
```

Part C (review P2) repaired a mixed model-api block; the previously api-less
model resolves through the backfilled provider api, `getError()` is clean, and
re-running reports no changes.

### Static checks

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean (also enforced by pre-commit)
- `oxlint` — clean

## Scope & honest notes

- Overlaps siblings #102148 / #102154 (same issue, Google plugin doctor
  contract), which earlier review found incomplete (missing `input`
  normalization / compile blockers). This PR does all three fixes with the
  mixed-api idempotency case covered.
- Covers the issue's first problem (migration gap). The second — fast-failing
  an unavailable fallback candidate instead of the 120s watchdog — lands in the
  core model-resolution path and needs a live credentialed google repro; it is
  intentionally tracked on the canonical issue, not in this PR.
- Migrations run under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`, not automatically at
  startup.
- Scoped to `google` / `google-vertex`; `google-antigravity` /
  `google-gemini-cli` are out of scope (not named in the issue).
